boundary.start: Invocation on an already constructed Nanobot instance, before per-call runtime selection.
boundary.terminal: The foreground await returns RunResult, raises an exception, or is cancelled.
boundary.command_short_circuit: A handled command may return before context construction, model inference and the normal save/respond stages; the command handler has its own persistence and effects.
boundary.same_session_serialization: process_direct serializes with bus turns using the same session lock; model selection and optional MCP connect occur before that lock.

input_schema.description: Nanobot.run arguments. This is a declaration of the Python SDK surface, not a new runtime JSON validator. Non-null hooks require Python objects.

message.description: User message; slash commands may short-circuit model inference.

ephemeral.description: Controls session persistence/compaction policy; does not sandbox or roll back tool side effects.

attributes.description: Caller-owned context, kept separate from trusted message metadata; Python Mapping values may need serialization.

field_semantics.content: Response text, or empty string when no outbound response/content is returned; no non-empty guarantee.
field_semantics.tools_used: Authoritative after_run capture lists successful tool events; not a complete list of attempts or failures.
field_semantics.messages: Captured runner message list; may be empty for command short-circuits. Not a guaranteed complete external event trace.
field_semantics.usage: Captured provider token/accounting values; may be empty.
field_semantics.stop_reason: Captured runner status, nullable when runner hooks did not execute (e.g. command shortcut). completed can include refusal/content-filter text. After injection-driven continuation, an earlier error status may remain alongside recovered final content.
field_semantics.error: Nullable captured diagnostic text; inspect together with stop_reason and content/history. None does not prove task success or rule out earlier recoverable tool errors. Non-null error can retain an earlier failure after continuation produces a later answer; it is not an exact classification of that final answer.
field_semantics.metadata: Outbound metadata copied by SDK; arbitrary keys, not a stable business result schema.

branches.condition: Foreground call returns a RunResult; inspect all fields and external acceptance criteria.
Runner terminal error response is converted to RunResult; stop_reason=error and error contains diagnostic text on that path.
A fatal tool error terminates the runner, absent continuation/recovery; stop_reason=tool_error, not necessarily a raised SDK exception.
stop_reason=max_iterations; a no-tools finalization pass or fallback response may be produced. error may remain null.
Terminal blank model output after recovery produces stop_reason=empty_final_response and a diagnostic response.
Handled command bypasses the runner; capture fields can remain at defaults, including stop_reason=null.
When process_direct returns None, SDK content is empty; capture state may still be populated.

exceptions.native_mechanism: Python raise/async cancellation; Nanobot.run does not wrap all exits in a RunResult.

branches.condition: Both model and model_preset supplied, or channel=system; model/config validation may raise earlier.
Uncaught runtime selection, MCP, session, hook, provider, persistence or finalization failure; subtype/message not fixed.
Cancellation propagates; it is not a guaranteed RunResult(stop_reason=cancelled).

capture_schema.description: Evaluator-owned observation envelope, not a native Nanobot response. Capture at the SDK call boundary; cancellation needs separate handling from Exception.

tool_dispatch.registry_return_type: Any; implementation-specific. No universal successful result shape is inferred.
tool_dispatch.error_marker: ToolResult.is_error; a plain string beginning with Error: is not by itself a builtin tool failure marker.
tool_dispatch.event_observation: AgentHookContext.tool_events in runner hooks; not a top-level RunResult field and not emitted as StreamEvent by run().

error_categories.observation: prepare_call returns error; tool implementation is not called.
prepare_call coerces/casts and validates parameters; rejected arguments do not call the implementation.
ToolResult.is_error produces an error event in the runner.
Ordinary Exception becomes a registry ToolResult.error or a runner error event; handling differs by entrypoint.
Repeated external lookup/workspace violation guards can reject or escalate; do not infer recoverability from fail_on_tool_error alone.
Cancellation and control-flow BaseException can propagate; hooks may also raise outside the implementation catch.

tool_dispatch.fail_on_tool_error: False generally returns tool errors to the model for possible recovery; True can terminate with tool_error. Policy guards and continuations also affect the terminal outcome.

retry.description: The registry does not automatically retry an implementation call. The model may request a new call; provider retries and tool-internal retries are separate.

remaining_gaps: No per-tool complete successful result schemas or business error-code taxonomy.
No universal rollback, exactly-once, idempotency, batch or permission-confirmation guarantees.
No implemented exception capture envelope in this exporter; evaluator must provide observation.
No real model/service execution evidence, business acceptance oracle or scenario fixtures.
Streaming lifecycle and global completion of spawned/background work are outside this boundary.
